title: The Stone's Hidden Linguistic Bedrock

features.name: the glyph rows
features.desc-on-touch: Stone markers arranged in lines, each one a word the water taught to the bedrock. The grammar is old—older than language itself.

features.name: the settling pool
features.desc-on-touch: Where water has learned to be still enough to listen. Here, it teaches the stone its own grammar—a language made of pressure and time.

features.name: the laminated record
features.desc-on-touch: Layers of stone, each one a page in a book the earth is writing. Water has marked every page with meaning the stone is learning to read.

features.name: the root-voice transmission
features.desc-on-touch: Veins of quartz where roots have grown close and started to speak the stone's language back to it. Both are learning each other's grammar now.

features.name: the deepest teaching place
features.desc-on-touch: A chamber where stone and water meet without interruption. Nothing speaks here anymore. Everything speaks. The grammar is complete.

inscription: where the stone learned that water speaks all the languages at once
